meta.subtitle: Now profitable and generating cash, but credit risk, rising funding costs and concentrated voting control justify caution

analystCommentary:
Pagaya turned profitable in FY25, with net income attributable to shareholders of $81.4 million against a loss of $(401.4) million in FY24, and it now generates substantial free cash flow.

At $18.01 on October 2, 2026 the shares sit between the 52-week low of $10.40 and the high of $32.04. The Street is uniformly positive (see Valuation).

We are more cautious. Pagaya's revenue depends on investors continuing to fund the loans its Partners originate, revenue is growing more slowly than volume, and the company holds risk retention positions that expose it directly to credit losses (see Risks).

We rate PGY HOLD.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Pagaya Technologies Ltd. is a technology company that uses data science and AI to help financial institutions approve more loan applications. Its Partners, ranging from financial technology companies to incumbent banks, auto finance providers and residential real estate service providers, send applications they would otherwise decline to Pagaya's network. Loans originated with Pagaya's help are bought by Financing Vehicles, including Pagaya-sponsored asset-backed securitizations and forward flow arrangements with third-party investors.

Pagaya earns network AI fees, contract fees, interest income and investment income. Its main products include Decline Monetization, Dual Look and First Look, along with customer acquisition tools.

The company was founded in 2016 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

thesis.body: Pagaya has shown it can grow and be profitable, and its multiples are low. But its earnings depend on credit markets: investor appetite for consumer loans, the cost of funding and the performance of the loans it helps originate. Our probability-weighted fair value implies upside, but the downside in a credit downturn is large enough that the reward/risk falls short of a BUY (see Valuation).

catalysts: Further diversification of the investor funding base.
Stable credit performance in Pagaya-sponsored securitizations.
risks: A rise in consumer credit losses.
Higher funding costs or weaker investor demand.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $1.3B, up 25.6% on our data; the 10-K reports revenue and other income of $1,301.4 million, a 26% growth rate, so the two sources agree. Operating margin improved from -3.2% in FY23 and 6.7% in FY24 to 20.9% in FY25, and diluted EPS turned positive at $0.93 from -$5.66. The 10-K credits the rise in Adjusted EBITDA, to $371.0 million from $210.4 million, to FRLPC improvement initiatives and disciplined cost management.

In the second quarter of 2026 revenue was $365.6M, up 15.1%, and operating margin was 28.9%.

The counter-case: revenue growth is slowing from the FY25 rate, and the trailing net margin of 9.6% is well below the operating margin. The 10-K itself warns that growth rates have slowed and may continue to slow.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Our data does not report total debt or a current ratio for FY25, so we cannot assess leverage from the summary figures. Total equity recovered to $0.6B at the end of FY25 from $0.4B a year earlier, as the company returned to profit, which strengthens its capacity to absorb losses.

The offsetting exposure is risk retention. The 10-K filed in March 2026 says these holdings increased during 2025 as a result of ABS issuances, and that the magnitude of potential losses increased with them. That means Pagaya is not a pure fee business: if loans in its securitizations perform poorly, it bears part of the loss directly.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $224.7M in FY25, a 17.8% FCF margin, after negative or thin margins in FY22 to FY24. The trailing FCF yield is 16.8%. Capital expenditure is small.

The swing to strong cash generation is a major change in the business. Its durability depends on funding markets staying open, so we would want to see it sustained through a period of credit stress before relying on it.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $18.01 PGY trades at 12.9x trailing earnings, 4.9x NTM earnings, ~4.4x FY27E earnings and 1.1x trailing sales.

Consensus EPS of $3.70 for FY26E and $4.13 for FY27E is far above FY25 diluted EPS of $0.93. The consensus basis is not stated; the company reports Adjusted EBITDA and other non-GAAP measures, so the estimates may be on an adjusted basis, and the forward multiples may flatter the stock on a GAAP view. The trailing P/E is the more conservative anchor.

All 11 covering analysts rate Buy, with a consensus target of $28.91, a median of $27.00 and a range of $23.00–$36.00.

We have no peer multiples to compare against. In our view, the low multiple reflects credit and funding risk as well as growth expectations.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Network Volume keeps growing, credit performance stays stable and funding costs ease. The market re-rates Pagaya as a durable earner, taking the shares into the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Pagaya delivers close to consensus, funding remains available at today's costs, and the multiple recovers modestly. The shares settle just below the lowest Street target of $23.00.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Consumer credit deteriorates, losses rise on risk retention holdings and investors pull back from funding. Network Volume and earnings fall, and the shares return toward the 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it assumes only that today's conditions persist. Bear carries more weight than Bull because the MD&A already reports a higher cost of capital and the 10-K reports larger risk retention exposure. Bull needs easier funding as well as continued growth.

The result is a weighted fair value of $20.70, an expected upside of +14.9% and a bear-case downside of -38.9%. The expected upside is meaningful, but the bear-case downside is too large relative to it for a BUY.

Our $18–$26 target range brackets Base. Its low end is today's price; its high end, just below the Street median target, is where we think the shares could trade if the Bull conditions begin to appear.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Pagaya reports a single segment. Management describes two sides of the business: a fee-generating product suite and a capital efficiency side that funds the assets. The main operating measure is Network Volume, the gross dollar value of assets originated by Partners with the assistance of Pagaya's AI technology.

moatFactors.name: Data network
moatFactors.body: Pagaya says it has evaluated more than $4.2 trillion in application volume since inception, and that more data leads to more efficient pricing. The MD&A also notes that its machine learning models are static and change only through human testing, validation and governance, so the data advantage is realized through deliberate model updates rather than continuous learning.

moatFactors.name: Partner integration
moatFactors.body: Once integrated, Partners tend to scale origination volume on the network, and the MD&A says Pagaya's share of their originations tends to increase over time. The counter-case is that Partners can add other providers.

moatFactors.name: Funding network
moatFactors.body: Pagaya has diversified its investor base: its top 5 investors accounted for approximately 44% of total funding in the six months ended June 30, 2026, against 52% a year earlier. Funding remains its point of dependence, since revenue relies on investor appetite.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. The data network and Partner integrations give Pagaya an advantage in underwriting declined applications. Its dependence on outside investors to fund the loans means the business is only as durable as its access to capital.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$1.5B, up 16%, and FY27E revenue of $1.7B. That is a slower pace than FY25 and, in our view, a realistic one given the trend below.

Network Volume rose to $3,535 million in the second quarter from $2,648 million, faster than revenue. Less revenue per dollar of volume is consistent with the MD&A's statement that conversion ratios have been adjusted to meet investor return expectations; in our view, volume growth alone overstates the earnings momentum.

Pagaya continues to introduce new asset types, products and services. In our view, these matter most if they bring in new funding sources, since funding, not Partner demand, is the binding constraint.
The MD&A says the cost of capital has risen. Until that reverses, we expect growth to come at lower margins per unit of volume.

management.leadership: Gal Krubiner is Chief Executive Officer, and the Board is led by an independent Chairman, Avi Zeevi, per the proxy statement dated July 2026. Mr. Yulzari, Mr. Pardo and Ms. Rosen also serve on the Board and are employed by the company. Management has delivered the shift to profitability and positive cash flow shown in Financials.
management.capitalAllocation: Pagaya pays no dividend, and our data shows no repurchase amounts for FY21 to FY25. Its main capital decision is how much risk retention it holds in its securitizations, which supports funding but exposes the balance sheet to credit losses. In our view, holders should watch whether risk retention keeps rising relative to the business.
management.governance: Per the proxy statement dated July 2026, the Board determined that Avi Zeevi, Alison Davis, Jason Gardner, Harvey Golub, Asheet Mehta and Dan Petrozzo are independent director nominees, while Mr. Krubiner, Mr. Pardo, Mr. Yulzari and Ms. Rosen are not because they are employed by the company. The Board held six meetings during fiscal year 2025. Under the Israel Companies Law and its own policy, Pagaya's Audit and Finance Committee determines whether a transaction with a covered person is an extraordinary transaction. The independent Chairman is a positive, but the voting control set out in Insider ownership limits what independent directors can do.
management.insiderOwnership:
Pagaya has a dual-class structure. As of June 15, 2026 Gal Krubiner held 43.3% of total voting power, Avital Pardo 42.5% and Yahav Yulzari 40.1%, mostly through Class B Ordinary Shares. The individual figures overlap, which the excerpt does not explain. All directors and executive officers as a group held 81.8% of total voting power but only 3.5% of the Class A Ordinary Shares. Oak HC/FT Partners II, L.P. held 5.7% of the Class A Ordinary Shares.

For public holders, this means insiders can decide shareholder votes, while the excerpt does not show how large their economic stake is relative to that control. Outside shareholders have little say over strategy or governance.

idiosyncratic: Credit performance: the 10-K warns that poor performance of the Financing Vehicles would likely reduce revenue, net income and cash flow, and impair Pagaya's ability to raise capital.
Risk retention: the larger holdings described in Financials increase Pagaya's direct exposure to loan losses.
Funding: the MD&A says the conflict between Israel, the U.S. and Iran that erupted in February 2026 has increased Pagaya's cost of capital and may diminish investor appetite for risk assets.
Control: the voting structure set out in Management limits the influence of public shareholders.
risks.systemic: The MD&A says elevated interest rates and inflation increase borrowing costs and could lead to higher delinquencies, defaults and charge-offs, reducing investor returns and demand for assets from the platform. Regional bank stress or broader liquidity problems could disrupt funding flows. Pagaya's earnings are therefore closely tied to the consumer credit cycle.

body: HOLD, target range $18–$26, based on the scenarios in Valuation.

We would move to BUY on evidence that funding costs are easing and credit performance is holding through a period of stress, or on a lower share price. We would turn more cautious if delinquencies rise or if investors pull back from Pagaya's securitizations.
